Europe faces severe drought impacting crops and economy

Much of Europe is experiencing a severe drought due to soaring temperatures and heatwaves, leading to significant impacts on agriculture and the broader economy. Farmers across the continent are reporting crop failures, including potatoes, corn, and cereals, with some harvests potentially being the worst on record. The drought is also affecting livestock, with overheating sheep and parched fields. The economic consequences are substantial, with one bank warning of a potential 1 percent reduction in EU GDP by 2026. Some areas are seeing early grape harvests, while others are experimenting with drought-resistant crops and water conservation methods.
